title: Consolidate model asset ingestion and simplify tokenizer contract
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We have accumulated several small, overlapping ad-hoc handlers in the model ingestion pipeline: multiple weight manifest parsers (v1/v1a/v1-legacy), a per-checkpoint sharder mapping that duplicates logic from the serving runtime, and a tokenizer adapter layer with brittle handshake semantics. These redundancies increase test surface, slow boot times for large models, and make it hard to reason about backwards compatibility when we change sharding or tokenizer metadata formats.

Goals:
- Introduce a single canonical asset manifest (manifest-v2) that normalizes weight shard metadata and tokenizer pointers.
- Move tokenizer contract to a minimal deterministic interface (TokenizerDescriptor) that is loaded as part of model assets and does not require runtime probing.
- Remove duplicated shard mapping logic from loader by producing a normalized ShardIndex during ingestion that the runtime can consume without additional negotiation.
- Provide backwards-compatible shim that upgrades v1 manifests to manifest-v2 at ingestion time (non-destructive).

Non-goals:
- Not changing serving runtime execution kernels or tokenizer implementations themselves. This ticket is ingestion/contract work only.

Acceptance criteria:
- New manifest-v2 samples pass unit tests and round-trip tests against fuzzed manifest inputs.
- Ingestion path emits a single canonical directory layout and a ShardIndex file for every model.
- TokenizerDescriptor replaces runtime tokenizer probing: runtime can load model with no additional tokenizer handshake in 95% of test cases.
- Boot time for a 60B model on CI reduced by >= 15% in the cold-start ingestion+load path.
- Backwards-compatible upgrade succeeds for at least three internal checkpoints (gpt-6b-open, rw-13b, internal-experimental-128k).

Design overview:
- Add manifest-v2 schema that consolidates weight shards (start/length/checksum), shard owner hints, and tokenizer references (type, vocab-file, byte-encoder-id).
- Implement a single ingestion API: ingest_model_assets(path) -> {canonical_layout, shard_index.json, tokenizer_descriptor.json}. The implementation will be in the loader service and run as a pre-flight step for hosted uploads and CI model registry publish flows.
- TokenizerDescriptor is intentionally minimal: {type, version, vocab_uri, merges_uri (optional), byte_encoder_id, compatibility_flags}. The runtime will validate byte_encoder_id on load and fall back only if mismatch is detected.
- Migration shim: ingest will detect legacy manifests and materialize manifest-v2 next to existing artifacts; original files are kept for audit.

Migration plan & rollout:
1) Merge schema and ingestion code behind feature flag ingest_v2 (runtime unaffected).
2) Run ingestion in CI for all newly published internal checkpoints for 2 weeks, gather metrics.
3) Run a batch ingestion for top-20 customer checkpoints in staging; validate tokenization outputs and model outputs against golden evals.
4) Enable default ingestion-v2 for new uploads; keep legacy paths for existing deployments for one release cycle.
5) After stability window, switch runtime to prefer shard_index.json and tokenizer_descriptor.json if present.

Risks & mitigations:
- Tokenizer mismatch causing subtle decoding differences -> mitigation: strict byte_encoder_id check + quick fallback path with telemetry alert and automatic rollback.
- Ingest rate causing CI regression -> mitigation: throttle background batch jobs and run on dedicated runners.
- Manifest conversion bugs -> mitigation: multiple hydration unit tests, property-based tests, and deterministic round-trip verification.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for schema validation and conversion logic.
- Integration tests that ingest small/medium/large models and validate load in a sandboxed runtime.
- Performance benchmark harness to measure cold-start and ingestion time.
- Add regression prompts to the eval harness to ensure tokenization parity for migrated models.

Metrics we'll track:
- Ingestion latency p50/p95 for 1GB/10GB/100GB model artifacts.
- Cold-start wall clock from ingestion start -> runtime ready.
- Percentage of loads that used tokenizer_descriptor vs runtime probe.
- Number of fallback tokenizer fallbacks in staging/production.

Notes:
- This ticket consolidates several prior efforts and should simplify follow-ups like cached prefix mapping and shard-level parallel download optimization.
- We will coordinate with SDK and Private teams to ensure the asset layout is compatible with Dedicated/Private deployment upload flows.
comments: 2025-02-10 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after spike. Spike notes in attachment. Initial approach leans toward minimal TokenizerDescriptor to keep runtime surface area small.

2025-02-14 Marco Reyes: Implemented prototype ingest_v2 writer. Verified manifest-v2 schema can represent existing shards for rw-13b. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4732
2025-02-18 Design review - Sofia Kim: Reviewed TokenizerDescriptor; requested adding compatibility_flags to capture known byte-encoder quirks and documented impact on client SDKs.
2025-02-22 QA - Daniel Moore: Ran ingestion on gpt-6b-open, found one mismatch in merges_uri resolution for legacy s3 prefixes. Added s3 URL normalization step to ingest_v2.
2025-02-28 Marco Reyes: Performance run on CI shows ~18% reduction in cold-start for ingest+load on sample 60B model when shard_index is used. Need additional integration tests for private uploads.
2025-03-03 Security - Priya Singh: Confirmed no secret materialization in manifest-v2; recommend adding audit log entry when ingest performs automatic conversion.
